operational-example.copy: Use Skeleton when content structure is known but data is still loading, refreshing, or hydrating. Skeleton preserves layout expectation without pretending the data is ready.

scenario.title: Dashboard loading structure
scenario.meta: Cards, rows, and map modules loading in place
rationale: It keeps the expected layout stable while data arrives.
It communicates loading without inventing content or fake progress.
The loading state stays tied to the surface that will receive real content.

items.rule: Matches the future content area without becoming a card style by itself.
Represents a title, row, media block, metric, or control placeholder.
Uses spacing and proportions from the real layout.
Uses subtle shimmer only while loading and respects reduced motion.
Exposes loading context for assistive technologies when the parent region is busy.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, loaded, paused, stale, loading, default
items: Use aria-busy on the region that owns the loading content.
Do not expose decorative bones as separate controls.
Replace Skeleton with real content as soon as content is available.
Use Progress Indicator instead when a real progress value exists.

variants.copy: Skeleton variants describe the exact content structure being reserved: text, title, circle, card, pill, row, media, chart, and table. Use the smallest bone that matches the future content, then compose it inside Card, List, Table, or a parent pattern.

states.copy: Skeleton states describe loading availability: default, loading, stale, paused, loaded, disabled. Error should replace Skeleton with recovery messaging.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines the shape of the future content. State defines whether the placeholder is actively loading, stale, paused, loaded, or unavailable.

full-width.copy: Skeleton should fill the same width as the content it reserves. Full-width skeletons are useful for rows, modules, and cards; compact skeletons should remain compact.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Responsive skeletons keep the future layout stable. On small screens, stack bones vertically; on wider screens, preserve row and card rhythm.

viewport-organization.copy: Use Skeleton where real content will appear. If the wait has measurable progress, use Progress Indicator. If loading fails, replace Skeleton with recovery.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Stack skeleton bones inside the same card or row that will receive content.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Preserve card rhythm and avoid layout shift during data hydration.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use row or table skeletons for dense work queues; use table where the container preserves column width.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify variant, line count, state, full-width behavior, reduced motion, and whether Skeleton is still the right component instead of Progress Indicator.

api-foundations.copy: Skeleton API exposes variant, lines, rows, columns, state, label, and full-width behavior while Design System owns shimmer, reduced motion, layout rhythm, density, and loading semantics.

props.name: label
props.notes: Loading context for the owning region.

props.name: lines
props.notes: Number of text or row bones.

props.name: rows
props.notes: Number of table rows when variant is table.

props.name: columns
props.notes: Number of table columns when variant is table.

props.name: busy
props.notes: Sets aria-busy for the loading region.

props.name: state
props.notes: Maps loading, stale, paused, loaded, and disabled state treatment.

props.name: fullWidth
props.notes: Lets the placeholder fill the owning region when the future content is full-width.

props.name: width
props.notes: Optional placeholder width for direct structural bones.

props.name: height
props.notes: Optional placeholder height for direct structural bones.

groups.title: Use
items: Reserve the real content structure while data loads.
Use Skeleton for unknown duration loading.
Keep motion subtle and remove it for reduced motion.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use Skeleton when a progress value exists.
Do not show Skeleton after loading fails.
Do not invent random gray blocks that do not match the future layout.

groups.title: Review
items: Confirm aria-busy on the owning region.
Replace Skeleton with real content or recovery as soon as state changes.

mustTest: Skeleton is replaced on loaded or error
rejectIf: Skeleton appears without a known future structure.
A real progress value exists but Skeleton is used instead.
The placeholder remains after content loads.
Raw color, spacing, or motion values are used.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Skeleton as structural loading: agents can use it when future content shape is known but data is missing, while humans confirm whether the wait needs progress, recovery, or a larger loading pattern.
canDecide: Use Skeleton for unknown-duration loading with known layout structure.
Match variant to future content: text, row, card, media, chart, or table.
mustAsk: The system knows real progress value or remaining steps.
Loading can fail, be retried, cancelled, or recover.
The future layout is unknown or still being designed.
rejectIf: Skeleton replaces error, empty, or recovery messaging.
Placeholder shapes do not match the future content.
Decorative bones become focusable or announced as real content.
miel.handoff: I am using Skeleton because content structure is known but data is loading. I need confirmation on future layout, loading ownership, reduced motion, and when to replace it with content, progress, or recovery.
